macro_context.market_sentiment: Risk-off on May 4, 2026: Dow -1.13% (-557pts to 48,941), S&P 500 -0.41% to 7,200, Nasdaq -0.19% to 25,067. UAE intercepted Iranian missiles (first activation since US-Iran ceasefire), sending oil surging and reversing the record closes seen on May 1. 10-yr Treasury yield jumped to 4.45%; mortgage rates back above 6.5%.
macro_context.fed_outlook: FOMC held benchmark rate at 3.50%-3.75% on April 29, 2026 (Powell's likely final meeting as chair). Unusual 8-4 dissent split — three members wanted to drop future-cut language, one Trump appointee dissented for immediate cut. Markets pricing in no changes rest of 2026 and into 2027; inflation cited as elevated partly due to energy price increases.
macro_context.geopolitical: US-Iran conflict remains the dominant risk: UAE missile intercept on May 4 escalated tensions, oil prices spiked, Strait of Hormuz closure risk cited by IMF. IMF lowered global growth to 3.1%, inflation at 4.4%. Additional risks: US intervention in Venezuela, NATO-Greenland tension, ongoing tariff uncertainty, and midterm elections.

ticker_news.headline: Seagate Q3 FY2026 earnings: revenue $3.11B (+44.1% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $4.10 (beat by 17.1%); stock surged ~24% the week of Apr 28
Q4 FY2026 guidance: revenue ~$3.45B and EPS ~$5.00 — materially above prior estimates; nearline capacity almost fully allocated through 2027
Rosenblatt raised STX price target to $500 (from $370); Bank of America lifted target to $605 (from $450), both Buy-rated, citing AI infrastructure HDD demand
HAMR Mozaic 3+ qualified by five major cloud customers; Mozaic 4+ in development — Seagate ahead of WDC in HAMR technology deployment
Large data centers now represent 80% of Seagate revenue; eighth consecutive quarter of revenue growth driven by AI hyperscaler buildout

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Multiple significant PT raises post Q3 FY2026 earnings (Apr 29, 2026): Rosenblatt $370->$500 (later to $1,000 per 24/7WallSt), BofA $450->$605, Barclays $625->$750, Citi $480->$595->$740, Goldman Sachs $385->$700. Morgan Stanley Overweight maintained; selected STX as #1 IT hardware stock. Susquehanna upgraded from Negative to Neutral in Jan 2026. Strong Buy consensus: 11 buy, 2 hold, 0 sell from 13 analysts (TipRanks); 19 analysts Buy consensus (Yahoo). No recent downgrades.

web_context.competitor_activity: Western Digital (WDC) is primary competitor alongside Toshiba in HDD oligopoly. WDC holds ~52% nearline market share vs STX ~42%. WDC completed SanDisk spinoff in early 2026 to become a pure-play HDD company, also benefiting from AI storage supercycle. However, WDC HAMR is still targeting H1 2026 initial qualification (behind Seagate's Mozaic which is already in volume production). Citi raised both — WDC to $405 and STX to $595 — citing AI-driven pricing supercycle. Cantor Fitzgerald raised WDC PT to $500. Morgan Stanley picked STX over WDC as #1 IT hardware pick citing stronger margins. WDC trades at lower 19.95x forward P/E vs STX 23.12x, reflecting STX's technology/margin premium.
